sourceIssues.locator: Footnote 4 to the proof of Theorem 2.6, p.5, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "Being in a setup of (Λ⊗Q)-modules, the hypotheses of [12, Lem. 15.13] hold."
sourceIssues.correction: Working with Λ⊗Q secures only one hypothesis of Kato's Lemma 15.13, that 2 and the order of Δ are invertible in the residue field. The other, that K is not contained in Q(ζ_{p^∞}), fails for K = Q(i) or Q(√−2) with p = 2, and for K = Q(√−p) with p ≡ 3 mod 4. In those cases the proof should use Kato's variant 15.14, with G_∞ replaced by G′_∞ = Gal(Q(ζ_{p^∞})/K), as Kato himself does in 15.15 and 15.17.
sourceIssues.reason: Kato's Lemma 15.13 (Astérisque 295, p.264) opens with "assume K is not contained in Q(ζ_{p^∞})". It also assumes that 2 and the order of Δ are invertible in the residue field of p, which is the hypothesis the footnote secures. The excluded case is exactly where the paper applies Theorem 2.6. Theorem 1.2 uses p = 2 and the congruent number curve, with K = Q(i) = Q(ζ_4). Remark 3.6(i) uses p = 3 and K = Q(ζ_3). Kato's 15.14 states the modified lemma, and his proofs of 15.15 and Proposition 15.17 say they go through with it. The equality step of E2 uses only the conclusions of the lemma, so it goes through too. The proof body cites §15 as a whole, which includes 15.14, so Theorem 2.6 stands and only the footnote is wrong.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, p.6, in arXiv 2506.03465v2 (11 October 2025), the version read; the same in v1 (4 June 2025)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let ψ : A_K^×/K^× → K^× be the Hecke character associated to E/K."
sourceIssues.correction: ψ : A_K^×/K^× → C^×, whose values on ideals prime to its conductor lie in K.
sourceIssues.reason: A continuous character of the idele class group of infinity type (−1, 0) (§2.2.5 with k = 2) restricts to z ↦ z^{−1} on C^×, so it does not take values in K^×. The K^×-valued algebraic character of E is defined on A_K^× and is not trivial on K^×. Kato 15.7, which the paper follows, defines Hecke characters as maps C_K → C^×. Only the identity L(s, E/K) = L(s, ψ)L(s, ψ̄) is used.
